title.title: Hindman's finite sums and products conjecture
title.subtitle: Claim: every finite colouring of $\mathbb N$ has $m$-element sets whose subset sums and products all share one colour

plain: Paint every whole number one of a few colours: some sets have all their sums and products in one colour

panels.caption: the case $m = 2$: four numbers, one colour

beats.text: Colour the positive integers with finitely many colours. Can sums and products share one?
Even $\{x, y, x+y, xy\}$ was open over $\mathbb N$; Alweiss had done the rationals
The claim: sets of every finite size $m$, with no bound on how large they are

steps: Build numbers from far-apart blocks, so products share a colour

achievement.label: Hindman's finite sums and products conjecture (1979)
statement: \forall\, r\text{-colouring of } \mathbb N,\ \forall m:\ FS(A) \cup FP(A) \text{ in one colour}
achievement.context: Moreira (2017) had $\{x, x+y, xy\}$; Bowen–Sabok and Alweiss worked over $\mathbb Q$
achievement.note: Finite sets only: the infinite version is false (Hindman 1980)
